method: Every height is a multiple of the pen's writing width. The nib width (0.2 to 10 mm) is multiplied by the body ratio (1 to 10 nib widths) to give the x-height, by the ascender ratio (0 to 8 nib widths) to give the height of the ascender line above the x-height line, by the descender ratio (0 to 8 nib widths) to give the depth below the baseline, and by the gap ratio (0 to 10 nib widths) to give the space between the descender line and the next ascender line. The band from ascender line to descender line is the sum of the x-height, ascender and descender heights, and the baseline-to-baseline spacing is that band plus the gap, so a multi-line sheet is laid out by repeating the spacing. The slant is measured in degrees from vertical and limited to 0 to 45; the horizontal run of a slanted stem over a given height is that height multiplied by the tangent of the angle, so the tool reports the run over the body, the run over the whole band, and the slope as 1 to the reciprocal of that tangent: a 15 degree slant is 1 to 3.732, 30 degrees is 1 to 1.732 and 45 degrees is 1 to 1. Heights are rounded to 0.001 mm, and a slant of 0 degrees is reported as upright with no slope ratio rather than an infinite one. Blank fields, text, negative values and anything outside a field's range are rejected with a message naming the field and its range. The preview draws the four guidelines and three slant lines at a proportional scale, not at print size: the preview shows the proportions, the millimetre figures are the measurement. Slant is the lean of letter stems from vertical, not the angle of the nib's edge, and a pointed nib changes width along the stroke, so its figure is a starting body height rather than a nib multiple. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Broad-edge calligraphy is planned in nib widths: x-height is chosen as a number of nib widths and the ascender and descender are set as further multiples of the same writing width.
A guideline set carries four lines: ascender, x-height, baseline and descender, and baseline-to-baseline spacing is the full band plus any gap between lines.
A stem slanted by an angle from vertical shifts sideways by height times the tangent of that angle, so its slope reads 1 to the reciprocal of the tangent.
The tangents behind the reported slopes: 15 degrees is about 0.268 (1 to 3.73), 30 degrees is about 0.577 (1 to 1.73) and 45 degrees is 1 (1 to 1).
